designSequence.waveName: Generic Diagnostics, Error Handling, and Publication

purpose: Define the architecture of the reservation-backed OperationEntryPublisher protocol, its atomic acceptance/custody boundary, the mandatory per-Step specialization proof, and its Prefect integration boundary without selecting one universal storage, allocator, synchronization, or recovery implementation.

included: The roles and ownership boundaries of OperationEntryPublisher and PublicationReservation.
Reservation lifecycle and the one-attempt/one-entry authorization rule.
Atomic acceptance and the equivalence between reservation consumption and complete-entry retention.
No-fail ownership transfer and complete-entry capacity reservation.
Idempotent retry, status reconciliation, release preconditions, and distinct failure outcomes.
Recovery Owner and ambiguous-acceptance escrow obligations.
Identity generation, uniqueness, retention, and expiry proof required from each Step specialization.
The Single Step Publication specialization's role as a per-Step concrete policy/implementation contract.
The binding of the publication capability to Prefect execution without equating Prefect Task State with publication acceptance.
excluded: A universal in-memory queue, database, message broker, event bus, or persistence implementation.
A universal lock-free, lock-based, transactional, or distributed synchronization algorithm.
A generic Step Transaction Manager or global Publisher service.
A universal numeric reservation/status retention duration.
A universal Recovery Owner implementation or generic escrow storage service.
Any automatic retry, compensation, error resolution, or Step flow-control policy.

operationEntryPublisher.role: Step-specific Error Handling Composition-owned invocation-scoped capability that accepts and retains complete ErrorHandlingOperationEntry values.
operationEntryPublisher.authoritativeDelivery: The Publisher is the only authoritative delivery path for operation entries. The Error Handling Unit does not return a competing collection.

publicationReservation.role: Opaque, Publisher-issued capability that authorizes one complete entry for one specific handling operation attempt and secures the resources needed for the promised handoff.

singleStepSpecialization.role: Mandatory concrete per-Step specialization when the reservation-backed publication protocol is selected. It supplies the actual entry/result representation, no-fail transfer proof, Recovery Owner/procedure, identity generation, and status retention policy.
singleStepSpecialization.scope: It specializes the abstract protocol for one concrete Step. It is not a framework-wide default Publisher implementation or global policy.

architecturalOptions.name: DirectAppendWithoutReservation
architecturalOptions.description: Let the Error Handling Unit append completed operation results directly to a collection owned by Step Composition.
advantages: Simple implementation for a single-threaded, non-failing collection.
disadvantages: Does not secure capacity/resources before operation execution.
A dynamically sized entry may fail during allocation or transfer after the operation has already produced a result.
Does not define an atomic custody handoff or resolve ambiguous acceptance.
Cannot satisfy the existing Publisher/Reservation guarantees.

architecturalOptions.name: UniversalCentralPublisherService
architecturalOptions.description: Introduce a framework-wide Publisher service, global queue, or transaction manager shared by all Steps.
advantages: Could centralize storage and publication APIs.
disadvantages: Creates global ownership and lifecycle responsibilities not assigned to GPWCF.
Conflates Step-specific entry/result types and target scopes.
Introduces cross-Step contention, global identity, and recovery semantics without a generic contract.
Violates the invocation-scoped, Step-owned Publisher capability model.

architecturalOptions.name: ReservationBackedStepOwnedPublisher
architecturalOptions.description: Use an invocation-scoped Publisher owned by the concrete Step's Error Handling Composition. It grants a one-entry reservation before operation execution and atomically accepts the complete prepared entry.
advantages: Makes capacity/resource commitment precede operation execution.
Defines one atomic acceptance and custody-transfer point.
Supports idempotent retry and authoritative status reconciliation.
Keeps concrete storage/transfer/recovery policy with the Step specialization.
Avoids a global Publisher or generic transaction manager.
disadvantages: Requires a concrete no-fail transfer proof and Recovery Owner for each Step specialization.
Requires explicit retention/expiry and identity-generation policies.

selectedDesign.decision: Retain the existing reservation-backed, Step-owned OperationEntryPublisher protocol as the generic contract. Treat Single_Step_Publication_Specialization_Contract as a mandatory per-Step proof/implementation specialization whenever the protocol is selected.

ownership.publisherUser: The Error Handling Unit for one exact invocation and Association.
ownership.reservationIssuer: The concrete Publisher instance owned by the Step-specific Error Handling Composition.
ownership.reservationHolder: The Error Handling Unit that obtained the grant, subject to the exact capability transfer rules of the Step specialization.
ownership.acceptedEntryCustodian: Publisher/Step-specific Error Handling Composition after atomic acceptance.
ownership.preAcceptanceCustodian: The Error Handling Unit or the explicitly designated Step Recovery Owner, according to the exact custody-transfer point.
ownership.recoveryOwner: A named concrete Step-owned component/object defined by the Single Step Publication specialization; never an implicit local variable or the failed Publisher itself.

publisherCapability.scope: One Error Handling Unit invocation bound to one Step instance, Unit instance, Association, and association target.
publisherCapability.lifetime: The capability is valid only for the invocation/Association scope defined by the Step specialization. It must not be retained, transferred to another Unit/Association, or reused by a later invocation.
nonResponsibilities: Does not select or execute handling operations.
Does not schedule or serialize operation execution.
Does not define Step flow policy.
Does not own the Error Handling Unit instance.
Does not own or mutate source Error Occurrences or ErrorResult.

reservationContract.meaning: Opaque, Publisher-issued capability authorizing one complete entry for one specific handlingOperationAttemptIdentity.
reservationContract.capacityGuarantee: A successful grant secures the complete-entry retention capacity and all Publisher-controlled resources required for the promised final handoff. Reserving only a collection slot is insufficient when payload/entry construction or transfer may still allocate or fail.
reservationContract.oneEntryRule: One reservation authorizes exactly one complete logical ErrorHandlingOperationEntry for its bound operation attempt.
reservationContract.capabilityRule: The reservation is opaque and non-forgeable under the concrete Step representation. It cannot be used with another Publisher, invocation, Unit, Association, target, or operation attempt.
reservationContract.preExecutionRule: The Error Handling Unit must obtain a valid grant before starting the corresponding handling operation.
reservationContract.noImplicitRelease: Normal return, exception, cancellation, or invocation closure does not implicitly release a reservation.

validStates.meaning: The Publisher has granted the reservation and secured its promised capacity/resources. No entry has yet been accepted.
The matching complete entry has been atomically accepted and retained by the Publisher/Composition.
The reservation has been released without accepting an entry; its reserved capacity/resources are no longer held.

stateTransitions.cause: A valid reserve request receives ReservationGrant.
The matching complete entry is atomically accepted and retained.
The Unit releases the unused reservation after establishing that no result is pending publication, or after an explicit permitted custody transfer.

reservationLifecycle.terminality: Consumed and Released are terminal reservation lifecycle states. A reservation cannot transition from Consumed to Released or from Released to Consumed.
reservationLifecycle.queryOutcomeRule: Unknown, Indeterminate, Unavailable, InvalidCapability, and Expired are status-query outcomes, not additional reservation lifecycle states. A failed status query must not be mapped to Reserved, Released, Rejected, or definitely-not-accepted.
reservationLifecycle.retryRule: Reserved permits retry of the same logical immutable entry under the same reservation, subject to the Step recovery policy. Consumed proves acceptance and prohibits a second distinct entry. Released proves no entry was accepted under that reservation.

preconditions: Invocation is open for new reservations.
Caller is the Unit bound to this Publisher capability.
Attempt identity is new within its required scope.
Publisher can secure all promised complete-entry resources.
reserve.rejection: A normal rejection means no reservation was granted, no operation may begin under that attempt, and a later attempt requires a new handlingOperationAttemptIdentity.

preconditions: Reservation is valid and Reserved, or the request is an idempotent retry of the same already accepted logical entry.
Entry contains the actual handlingOperationIdentity assigned after grant and before execution.
Entry Step, Unit, Association, target, and invocation provenance exactly match the reservation binding.
Entry is fully prepared in the Step-specialized transfer representation before publish.

normalOutcomes.meaning: The complete entry is retained; reservation is Consumed; ownership transfers to Publisher/Composition.
Preconditions are not satisfied; no new entry was accepted and no ownership transfer occurred.
The Publisher breached a guarantee of a valid granted reservation or exposed an inconsistent acceptance state. It is not an ordinary rejection.

publish.idempotency: Repeating publish with the same reservation and same logical entry returns acknowledgement for the original acceptance without duplicate retention. Reusing a consumed reservation with different entry content is a conflict and must never be accepted.
publish.noPartialAcceptance: The Publisher must not expose partial entry content or consume the reservation without retaining the complete entry.

getPublicationStatus.purpose: Resolve ambiguous publish outcomes, including lost acknowledgements and exceptions after the request may have crossed the acceptance point.
rules: Status lookup is scoped to the exact issuing Publisher and reservation.
Consumed means the matching entry was accepted; do not republish as a new logical entry.
Reserved means the entry was not accepted and the same reservation may be used for the same logical entry under the Step recovery policy.
Released means no entry was accepted; a produced pending result with Released is a contract violation.
Query failure/Unavailable/Indeterminate leaves acceptance knowledge unresolved; preserve the complete result and reservation evidence.

preconditions: No operation result requiring publication is pending.
If a result was produced, its complete custody has first been explicitly transferred to the named Recovery Owner/alternative owner under the Step specialization.
release.rule: The Publisher does not infer release from normal return, exception, cancellation, or invocation closure.

atomicAcceptance.definition: One indivisible logical Publisher transition in which the complete matching entry becomes retained and its reservation becomes Consumed.
atomicAcceptance.linearizationPoint: The exact logical instant at which both complete-entry retention and reservation consumption become externally true.
atomicAcceptance.equivalence: Reservation.Consumed if and only if the matching complete entry has been accepted and the Publisher/Composition has assumed retention responsibility.
beforeAcceptance: Entry is not in the accepted-entry set.
Unit or Recovery Owner retains the complete recoverable result/entry.
afterAcceptance: Complete entry is retained by Publisher/Composition.
Reservation is Consumed and cannot authorize a different entry.
Later Unit exception or loss of acknowledgement does not revoke acceptance.
atomicAcceptance.implementationFreedom: A concrete implementation may use locks, preallocated slots, owning handles, a durable store, or another mechanism. It must expose behavior equivalent to one atomic transition and satisfy the no-fail transfer proof.
noFailTransferRequirement: All fallible result and entry construction occurs before publish.
The reserved resource covers the complete dynamically sized payload and all required metadata, not merely one collection slot.
The final transfer must not allocate, serialize, convert, clone, deep-copy, or invoke arbitrary user code.
The final ownership handoff must be guaranteed non-throwing by the concrete Step-specialized type/resource contract.
A preallocated owning entry envelope or pre-created owning handle may be used if its transfer is proven non-throwing.
A potentially throwing move is not considered safe without a concrete type-level guarantee.

custodyPhases.custodian: Error Handling Unit owns its execution resources; no operation result exists.
Error Handling Unit retains the complete result and prepared entry.
Named Step Recovery Owner accepts the complete result/entry through a verifiable transfer before Unit unwinding/release.
Named Recovery Owner/escrow retains a complete recoverable representation while acceptance knowledge remains indeterminate; it is marked non-publishable and must not be aggregated as accepted.
Step-specific Error Handling Composition/aggregate owner retains the accepted entry through ErrorHandlerResult and StepExecutionResult retention.

custodyAndRecovery.mandatoryRecoveryOwner: Every Step specialization using this protocol names a concrete Step-owned Recovery Owner, with identity, lifetime, storage/custody capability, and explicit transfer/reconciliation procedures. The failed Publisher itself is not the sole Recovery Owner for a Publisher Contract Violation.
ambiguousAcceptanceProcedure: Freeze the affected attempt; do not execute a replacement operation for the same logical attempt.
Preserve the complete result and prepared entry under Unit custody or transfer them to the Recovery Owner before exception unwinding or resource release.
Query authoritative Publisher status when safely available.
If Consumed, reconcile the original accepted entry and do not publish a duplicate.
If Reserved and Publisher guarantees remain trustworthy, retry only the same immutable entry under the same reservation.
If Released while a produced result is pending, classify a Publisher Contract Violation and retain the result under the Recovery Owner.
If acceptance remains Indeterminate/Unavailable, retain the complete result in escrow, prohibit a second publication/operation attempt, and follow the Step-specific reconciliation/escalation policy.
The escrow is not an accepted ErrorHandlingOperationEntry and must not be counted in ErrorHandlerResult.
Record final custody as Publisher accepted, Recovery Owner retained, explicitly transferred, or unresolved/escalated.
publisherContractViolationMinimumEvidenc: Violation identity and stable producer-owned code/category.
Publisher, invocation, reservation, Unit, attempt, and operation identities when known.
The protocol phase and violated guarantee/invariant.
Acceptance knowledge: definitely-not-accepted, definitely-accepted, or indeterminate.
Current result custodian or explicit custody-unresolved state.
Optional typed Diagnostic evidence; diagnostics do not replace any of the preceding facts.
prohibitedRecoveryShortcuts: Discarding a result because publish threw or returned no acknowledgement.
Treating status-query failure as proof of non-acceptance.
Releasing a reservation while a result is pending without explicit custody transfer.
Starting a replacement operation attempt while acceptance is indeterminate.
Publishing the same logical result to an alternate sink without deduplication and explicit ownership/aggregation rules.
Aggregating an escrow record as if it were an accepted entry.

identityRules: Every identity has a documented issuer, representation, uniqueness scope, stability, reuse/retirement, and replacement behavior.
handlingOperationAttemptIdentity is allocated before reserve and does not assert that operation execution started.
handlingOperationIdentity is allocated only after a valid reservation grant and before actual operation start.
A new actual execution receives a new handlingOperationIdentity.
An idempotent retry uses the same reservation and same immutable logical entry/acceptedEntryIdentity.
Identity values are not reused while any reservation, acknowledgement, status record, recovery record, accepted entry, or aggregate may still refer to them.
Publisher replacement receives a distinct publisherIdentity while prior records remain observable.
Native Prefect IDs are never substituted for any domain publication identity.

mustDefine: Retention/expiry for Reserved, Consumed, and Released status records.
Minimum status-query/idempotent-retry horizon after Unit invocation closure.
Retention through ErrorHandlerResult collection and StepExecutionResult integration.
How the Step proves no retry/status observer remains before terminal record reclamation.
Whether tombstones remain to prevent stale identity reuse/duplicate acceptance.
Unresolved/indeterminate escrow retention and escalation horizon.
Late query and stale capability behavior after expiry.
minimumRules: Do not remove status while acceptance is indeterminate or result custody is unresolved.
Consumed remains queryable until accepted-entry aggregation and all permitted retry observers are complete.
Released remains distinguishable from Unknown/Expired for the Step-defined late-request window.
Expired is never mapped to definitely-not-accepted.
Reclaimed identity values are not reused if stale references may still be observed.

identityAndRetention.noUniversalRetentionNumber: No numeric retention duration is prescribed across all Steps. Each Single Step Publication specialization chooses and justifies its concrete retention policy.

concurrencyAndOrdering.reserveAtomicity: Concurrent reserve calls must be coordinated so granted reservations cannot collectively exceed the concrete Publisher's available complete-entry retention capacity.
concurrencyAndOrdering.publishAtomicity: Concurrent publish calls must preserve one-entry-per-reservation and the atomic acceptance invariant.
concurrencyAndOrdering.sameReservation: Concurrent/repeated publish calls for one reservation and the same logical entry converge on one acceptance and one retained entry.
concurrencyAndOrdering.conflictingEntry: A different entry under an already consumed reservation is rejected as conflict/contract violation and is never accepted.
concurrencyAndOrdering.ordering: The Publisher guarantees the ordering explicitly stated by the concrete Step specialization. It does not impose semantic operation order or Step flow order.
concurrencyAndOrdering.sequenceNumber: If the concrete Publisher exposes a publication sequence, its monotonicity, scope, overflow, restart, and persistence behavior are defined by that specialization.
concurrencyAndOrdering.concurrencyPolicy: No universal lock, lock-free algorithm, queue, or concurrency count is mandated.

singleStepPublicationSpecialization.owner: Each concrete Step specialization that uses the reservation-backed Error Handling publication protocol.
singleStepPublicationSpecialization.notAUniversalImplementation: The specialization is a per-Step contract proving that the abstract protocol can be safely realized for the Step's actual THandlingOperationResult, entry type, concurrency, storage, and lifecycle. It is not a generic global Publisher implementation.
requiredProofSections: Concrete THandlingOperationResult and complete ErrorHandlingOperationEntry representation.
PublicationReservation concrete representation and one-entry capacity guarantee.
No-fail final ownership-transfer primitive and proof that all fallible work occurs before acceptance.
Recovery Owner identity, storage/lifetime, custody-transfer operation, and ambiguous-acceptance escrow.
Publisher status retention/expiry and late-query behavior.
Concurrency, ordering, duplicate/conflict, and idempotent retry behavior.
End-to-end traces for all mandatory normal, rejection, exception, contract-violation, and indeterminate-acceptance branches.
ErrorHandlerResult collection and StepExecutionResult integration proof.
singleStepPublicationSpecialization.acceptanceRule: A Step specialization is not qualified to use the publication protocol until every required proof section is concrete and all mandatory branches end in a known custodian or an explicitly represented unresolved/escalated state.

prefectIntegrationBoundary.executionPlacement: The Error Handling Unit invocation/operation may be wrapped in a Prefect Task inside the owning Step Subworkflow. The Publisher remains owned by the Step-specific Error Handling Composition.

capabilityBindingOptions.description: Pass or close over an invocation-scoped Publisher capability when the Unit Task and owning Step Composition share the same process/address space and the Prefect task execution path does not require unsupported serialization of the capability.
capabilityBindingOptions.qualification: Must be proven for the selected TaskRunner and result-persistence profile; not assumed merely because tasks belong to the same Flow.

capabilityBindingOptions.description: Pass a typed invocation-bound handle/reference that resolves to the exact Step-owned Publisher capability within the same worker process.
capabilityBindingOptions.qualification: Must not be backed by a global mutable registry or permit cross-invocation/Association lookup. Its lifecycle and resolution scope are explicit.

capabilityBindingOptions.description: Use an explicit IPC or service-backed capability only when the Unit operation executes in a different process/host from the owning Publisher.
capabilityBindingOptions.qualification: Requires a separately designed protocol preserving atomic acceptance, reservation, no-fail transfer or durable handoff, status reconciliation, identity, and recovery semantics. PHASE-02 does not qualify this mechanism.

integrationRules: The Prefect Task Run ID is operational evidence and does not replace publisherIdentity, invocationIdentity, reservationIdentity, attemptIdentity, operationIdentity, or acceptedEntryIdentity.
Prefect Task COMPLETED does not prove publication acceptance.
Prefect Task FAILED/CANCELLED does not prove publication rejection or non-acceptance.
A returned PublicationAccepted acknowledgement proves the Publisher's atomic acceptance according to the specialized protocol, independent of the later Task State.
If the Task fails after publish may have crossed the acceptance point, the Step recovery procedure queries Publisher status and preserves custody.
The Prefect integration must not serialize an in-process capability object across a process boundary unless the concrete capability/serializer contract explicitly supports it.
No generic Publisher server, transaction service, or remote registry is introduced by the Prefect integration.
qualificationLimits: PHASE-01/02 did not implement or qualify the production OperationEntryPublisher/PublicationReservation protocol.
No evidence establishes serialization/transport of Publisher capabilities across Prefect process workers.
No evidence establishes atomic acceptance, no-fail transfer, or escrow recovery under worker loss.
No multi-host Publisher/storage profile is qualified.
Production Error Handling Unit functional binding remains unqualified.

dependencyAndPackageAllocation.implementationOwnership: Concrete Publisher/Reservation implementation and Recovery Owner are Step-specific specialization/deployment concerns; the generic contract package does not supply one universal implementation.
dependencyAndPackageAllocation.prefectAllocation: Any Prefect capability wrapper or native Task binding is under integrations.prefect and depends inward on the generic and specialized publication contracts.

requiredGoverningContractChanges.change: No semantic change to the abstract protocol is proposed. Add an integration note that a Publisher capability may cross a Prefect Task boundary only through a proven in-process or specialized interprocess binding preserving invocation scope and atomic acceptance.
requiredGoverningContractChanges.reason: The current contract defines domain protocol semantics but does not prove how a capability is transported through the selected external runtime.
requiredGoverningContractChanges.approval: Requires architecture acceptance before source contract editing.

requiredGoverningContractChanges.change: No semantic weakening or generic default is proposed. Ensure each concrete Step specialization completes all no-fail transfer, Recovery Owner/escrow, identity-generation, status-retention, and mandatory branch-trace proof sections before implementation qualification.
requiredGoverningContractChanges.reason: The specialization is the proof obligation that makes the abstract protocol implementable for actual result types and resources.

requiredGoverningContractChanges.change: Keep Publisher/Reservation protocol contracts within optional MOD-CORE-SUPPORT-EH; do not create a mandatory global publication module.
requiredGoverningContractChanges.reason: Publication is part of the selected optional Error Handling capability and is Step-owned.

requiredGoverningContractChanges.change: Allocate publication protocol contracts under core.supporting_patterns.error_handling.publication and Prefect capability bindings under integrations.prefect.
requiredGoverningContractChanges.reason: Separates generic protocol contracts, Step-specific implementations, and runtime binding.

conformanceRequirements.requirement: The Publisher is owned by the Step-specific Error Handling Composition and is invocation/Association scoped.
A valid reservation is granted before the corresponding handling operation begins.
One reservation authorizes one complete entry for one attempt identity only.
A grant secures complete-entry capacity and all resources required for the promised handoff.
The complete entry is prepared before publish and the final ownership transfer is proven non-throwing by the Step specialization.
Atomic acceptance is one indivisible transition in which the complete entry is retained and the reservation becomes Consumed.
Reservation.Consumed if and only if the matching complete entry has been accepted and retained.
Same-reservation/same-entry retry is idempotent; same-reservation/different-entry reuse is never accepted.
Status query outcomes such as Unknown, Indeterminate, Unavailable, InvalidCapability, and Expired are not reservation lifecycle states.
Status-query failure does not prove non-acceptance and does not authorize result disposal or a replacement operation attempt.
A reservation is released only when no result is pending or after explicit verifiable custody transfer under the Step specialization.
Every Step using the protocol names a concrete Recovery Owner and defines ambiguous-acceptance escrow/reconciliation.
Every publication identity has explicit issuer, representation, uniqueness, stability, reuse, and retirement rules.
Publisher status retention supports all permitted retries, reconciliation, aggregation, and late queries.
Prefect State and Task Run IDs remain operational evidence and do not substitute for publication acceptance or domain identities.
No universal Publisher implementation, transaction manager, queue, database, or recovery service is introduced.

supports: Invocation-scoped Publisher ownership and binding.
Reservation before operation execution.
One reservation/one entry, idempotent retry, atomic acceptance, and status reconciliation.
Publisher Contract Violation distinct from PublicationRejection.
Accepted-entry retention and Publisher/Composition custody.
Opaque reservation identity, capacity guarantee, one-attempt binding, and Reserved/Consumed/Released lifecycle.
Query outcomes distinct from lifecycle states.
Release preconditions and no implicit release.
Mandatory per-Step no-fail transfer proof.
Explicit Recovery Owner and ambiguous-acceptance escrow.
Identity generation and status retention obligations.
Mandatory end-to-end protocol branch traces.
The Unit publishes each produced operation result through the invocation-bound Publisher.
The Unit does not return a competing collection of entries.
The Unit retains the result before acceptance and Publisher owns it after acceptance.
Quiescence requires all reservations/results to be consumed, released, or transferred to Recovery Owner.
Accepted entries remain independent of Unit lifetime.
Error Handling remains optional and Step-owned.
Publication is a specialized capability and does not imply error resolution.
ErrorHandlerResult aggregates accepted entries only.
The qualified deployment profile uses separate Stage Process Workers and Step/SPU execution within the Stage worker context.
Production Publisher capability transport and multi-host publication are not qualified.

acceptanceCriteria: The generic reservation/publication protocol remains Step-owned and optional with Error Handling.
Atomic acceptance and custody transfer have one unambiguous linearization point.
The reservation guarantees complete-entry resources before operation execution.
The final ownership handoff is proven non-throwing by every concrete Step specialization.
All normal, rejected, exceptional, idempotent, conflict, contract-violation, and indeterminate-acceptance paths preserve result custody.
Every concrete Step names a Recovery Owner and defines escrow/reconciliation and status retention.
Identity generation/reuse rules prevent stale references and duplicate acceptance.
The Prefect integration does not equate Task State with publication acceptance and does not serialize an unsupported capability across process boundaries.
No universal Publisher implementation, queue, database, transaction manager, or recovery service is introduced.
The design remains within the PHASE-01/02 qualification boundary and does not claim production publication binding is qualified.
No specialized source contract is modified by this artifact.

changeControl.authority: Wave 4 detailed design proposal. It becomes an implementation constraint only after architecture review and explicit acceptance.
changeControl.sourceContractPolicy: The existing OperationEntryPublisher_Contract.json, PublicationReservation_Contract.json, and Single_Step_Publication_Specialization_Contract.json remain unchanged until their integration clarifications and concrete Step proof are approved.
changeControl.implementationGate: Do not implement a Publisher or Reservation mechanism until the owning Step specialization has completed and passed the no-fail transfer, Recovery Owner, identity, retention, and end-to-end branch proof.
changeControl.nextStep: Validate all three Wave 4 files together for Diagnostic/Error/Failure/Outcome separation, optional Error Handling ownership, and publication custody invariants before proceeding to Wave 5.
